name: Chizuko Matsui
current_role: Shareholder of Matsui Securities (former controlling shareholder); no executive role found
profile: Chizuko Matsui (松井千鶴子) was the largest and controlling shareholder of Tokyo online broker Matsui Securities, holding about 58% of voting rights (directly and indirectly) in 2015. In 2016-17 she transferred shares to Maruroku Ltd, the founding family's asset-management company, after which she ceased to be a major/controlling shareholder. Wealth is shared with longtime president Michio Matsui.
interesting_fact: Matsui Securities, founded in 1931 as a tiny brokerage, reinvented itself in the mid-1990s as one of Japan's first online brokers; in Nov 2026 Japan Post Bank agreed to buy shares from Maruroku and become its largest shareholder.
notes: Extremely private; no public profile, interviews or role beyond shareholder filings (JPX disclosures e.g. https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/86280/140120161104430973.pdf). Exact family relationship to Michio Matsui not confirmed in sources. Not a podcast-likely guest; any approach would be via Matsui Securities/Maruroku.

name: Mireille Gillings
current_role: Founder, CEO & Executive Chair, HUYABIO International; Co-founder & Non-Executive Vice Chair, GHO Capital
profile: Montreal-born neurobiologist (PhD Radboud Nijmegen, postdocs at Bordeaux and Scripps) who founded San Diego-based HUYA Bioscience International in 2004 to in-license and develop novel drugs discovered in China. She co-founded London healthcare private-equity firm GHO Capital. Married to Sir Dennis Gillings, founder of Quintiles (now IQVIA), source of the shared family fortune.
interesting_fact: HUYABIO pioneered a model of bringing Chinese-discovered drug compounds to Western clinical trials; Fortune profiled her in 2010 as a China biotech pioneer.
deep_cut_fact: The company name HUYA combines the Chinese abbreviations for Shanghai (Hù) and Asia (Yà); before HUYA she was also a co-founder of MIR3, and she calls herself a 'serial entrepreneur'. She speaks French natively plus Mandarin.
notes: Styled Lady Mireille Gillings. Listed as UK on Sunday Times Rich List but based in San Diego. Healthcare/biotech focus; best route is HUYABIO contact form.

name: Michael Rees
current_role: Co-President and board member, Blue Owl Capital; Head of GP Strategic Capital platform
profile: Rees spent 2001-09 at Lehman Brothers (head of asset management strategy 2003-06), moved to Neuberger Berman in its 2009 management buyout as first COO of its alternatives unit, and founded Dyal Capital there, pioneering buying minority stakes in private equity firms. Dyal merged with Owl Rock in 2021 to form NYSE-listed Blue Owl, where he co-presides and runs GP Strategic Capital.
interesting_fact: Dyal/Blue Owl GP Strategic Capital has bought minority stakes in 60+ private equity firms and runs a sports fund with pieces of the NBA's Phoenix Suns, Sacramento Kings and Atlanta Hawks.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he holds a BS in mechanical engineering and a BA in political science from the University of Pittsburgh plus MIT master's degrees in mechanical engineering and technology policy; his family backs the Rees Chancellor Scholarship program at Pitt. He calls himself a proud Pittsburgh 'Yinzer'.
notes: Has done podcasts (Capital Allocators ep. 278, CAIS Live) and a PEI 'Off-duty' interview on how Dyal got its name and Guns N' Roses (https://www.privateequityinternational.com/off-duty-blue-owls-michael-rees-on-how-dyal-got-its-name-guns-n-roses-and-being-a-yinzer/, paywalled). Blue Owl is a major data-center financier, relevant to the podcast. Route via Blue Owl media.

name: Marc Zahr
current_role: Co-President and board member, Blue Owl Capital; Global Head of Real Assets
profile: Zahr co-founded Chicago net-lease real estate firm Oak Street in 2009 after roles at American Realty Capital, TM Associates and Merrill Lynch. Blue Owl bought Oak Street in Dec 2021 for $950M; as Blue Owl co-president he runs the Real Assets platform, chairs Blue Owl Real Estate Net Lease Trust and Blue Owl Digital Infrastructure Trust, and co-chairs STORE Capital.
interesting_fact: His business is the market leader in triple-net leases; Real Assets grew from $12.4B at acquisition to about $49B, and now includes Blue Owl's digital infrastructure (data center) trust, highly relevant to a data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He started Oak Street in 2009, in the aftermath of the financial crisis, with fellow American Realty Capital alumnus Jim Hennessey, and was named to Crain's Chicago Business 40 Under 40 in 2018.
notes: Has appeared on Alt Goes Mainstream (Future Proof fireside chat) discussing net lease and data centers: https://altgoesmainstream.substack.com/p/future-proof-citywide-replay-alt . Strong podcast fit (data-center financing). Co-founder detail sourced from LoopNet company profile: https://www.loopnet.ca/company/oak-street-real-estate-capital/chicago-il/lryn8jgl/

name: Jacques Merceron-Vicat
current_role: Honorary Chairman (Président d'honneur) and director, Vicat SA
profile: Born 1938, Jacques Merceron-Vicat is the patriarch of the family that controls Vicat, the listed French cement group founded in 1853 near Grenoble by Joseph Vicat, son of cement pioneer Louis Vicat. He led the group as chairman/CEO for decades before handing operations to son-in-law Guy Sidos (CEO 2008, chairman 2014); he remains honorary chairman with a board mandate running to 2030.
interesting_fact: The family's ancestor Louis Vicat discovered the principle of hydraulic binders in 1817 (the basis of modern cement), and Joseph and Louis Vicat built the world's first concrete bridge at Grenoble's Jardin des Plantes in 1855.
deep_cut_fact: When Guy Sidos became chairman in March 2014, the board named Jacques Merceron-Vicat honorary chairman; he had stepped back from operational control around age 70, passing the CEO role to his son-in-law in 2008, keeping the 170-year-old company under sixth-generation family control.
notes: Aged ~88, low public profile. Company now active in cement decarbonisation and alternative fuels (energy angle). Better podcast guest may be CEO Guy Sidos; approach via Vicat press office (named press officer as published in Vicat's July 2026 release).

name: Judith Neilson
current_role: Founder and director, White Rabbit Gallery (Sydney); philanthropist and Platinum Asset Management shareholder
profile: Zimbabwe-born former graphic designer and Sydney philanthropist whose fortune stems from her stake in Platinum Asset Management, the global equities manager co-founded by her ex-husband Kerr Neilson (divorced 2015). She founded and solely funds the White Rabbit Gallery of post-2000 Chinese contemporary art, backed the Phoenix arts spaces in Chippendale, and set up the A$100M Judith Neilson Institute for Journalism and Ideas.
interesting_fact: White Rabbit holds one of the world's largest collections of 21st-century Chinese art; in 2024 she said it held work by around 800 artists and 'there were 4,000 pieces the last time I counted'. Her interest began on trips to Beijing in the late 1990s.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 she endowed a Chair of Architecture at UNSW to develop housing solutions for displaced people such as climate refugees and disaster or conflict victims, and in 2017 a Chair of Contemporary Art at UNSW. She was made a Member of the Order of Australia (AM) in 2016.
notes: Private, rarely interviewed. Note: neilson.org.au (contact@neilson.org.au) is the Neilson Foundation run by ex-husband Kerr Neilson, NOT her - do not use. Best route is via White Rabbit Gallery or the Judith Neilson Institute. Arts/journalism focus rather than energy.

name: Roberto González Barrera
profile: Mexican billionaire who built Gruma/Maseca (corn flour and tortillas) and chaired Banorte. Died 25 August 2012 in Houston, Texas, aged 81.
notes: Deceased (2012), source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Gonz%C3%A1lez_Barrera . Name in input garbled ('Gonz_lez'); identity inferred from Forbes 1996 Mexico listing. Successor generation: son Juan González Moreno (Gruma).

name: Hinduja, Srichand, Gopichand
profile: Combined 1999 Forbes listing for brothers Srichand (S.P.) and Gopichand Hinduja, co-chairmen of the Hinduja Group. Both have died: S.P. Hinduja on 17 May 2023 and Gopichand Hinduja on 4 November 2025.
notes: Both deceased. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S._P._Hinduja and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gopichand_Hinduja . Surviving brothers Prakash and Ashok Hinduja and the next generation run the Hinduja Group (energy interests incl. Hinduja Renewables, power), if the journalist wants a living contact.

name: Somchai Bencharongkul
profile: Listed once (Hurun Global 2015) with wealth from Total Access Communication (DTAC), the Thai mobile operator founded in 1989 by the Bencharongkul family and merged into True Corporation in 2023. No source found confirming a family member named Somchai; the well-documented DTAC founder is Boonchai Bencharongkul (b. 1954), eldest of four siblings who sold most of their DTAC shares in 2005.
notes: Identity unverified: Thai and English searches for 'Somchai/สมชาย Bencharongkul' found nothing; may be a Hurun mislabel for Boonchai (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boonchai_Bencharongkul) or a lesser-known sibling. Family vehicle is Benchachinda Holding. Recommend confirming before outreach.

name: José Roberto Ermírio de Moraes
current_role: Member of the Ermírio de Moraes family controlling Votorantim (a José Roberto Ermírio de Moraes Filho sits on Votorantim S.A.'s board)
profile: Member of Brazil's Ermírio de Moraes family, controlling shareholders of the century-old Votorantim conglomerate (cement, metals, energy via Auren, banking, etc.), held through the family holding Hejoassu. Forbes listed him in 2021 as one of several family billionaires. Two family members share the name (José Roberto Ermírio de Moraes and his namesake 'Filho'), and the Forbes '-1' slug does not make clear which one.
interesting_fact: Votorantim's founding family is now in its sixth generation, with 184 members of whom 58 are shareholders; a 12-member family 'Hejoassu Board' sets long-term strategy and appoints the company board.
notes: Ambiguous identity: Forbes profile https://www.forbes.com/profile/jose-roberto-ermirio-de-moraes-1/ (2021). José Roberto Ermírio de Moraes Filho is listed on Votorantim S.A.'s 2025 board (chairman is Eduardo Vassimon). Confirm which family member before outreach. Votorantim has major renewable-energy interests (Auren Energia) - relevant to energy podcast.

name: Caspar Callerström
current_role: Partner, EQT AB (Stockholm); Group deputy CEO & COO 2016-2022
profile: Stockholm School of Economics graduate who joined Swedish private-equity firm EQT in 1996 and became a partner in 2004. He headed EQT Equity in Stockholm (2007-13), sat on its Equity Partners Investment Committee, and was group deputy CEO and COO from 2016 to 2022, steering the firm through its 2019 IPO; his billionaire status comes from his EQT AB shareholding.
interesting_fact: He is one of the founding members of a group of financial elites backing Stockholm football club Djurgårdens IF; EQT's listing has minted about seven billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: Before group management he worked hands-on in portfolio companies, holding directorships at Thule (the roof-box/bike-rack maker), Scandic Hotels, Munksjö, Nederman, Sanitec and Dahl International.
notes: Low media profile. EQT is a large infrastructure/data-center investor (e.g., EdgeConneX), relevant to podcast. Route via EQT press office.

name: Chang Chung-Hsing
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Apex Dynamics (Taichung, Taiwan)
profile: Chang Chung-Hsing (張重興) founded Taichung-based Apex Dynamics in 1987 as a maker of robotic arms and built it into one of the world's largest suppliers of high-precision planetary gearboxes used in automation and machine tools. Apex listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in 2022, making him a billionaire on Forbes' 2025 list.
interesting_fact: Apex also owns the Millennium Vee Hotel Taichung, run with Singapore's Millennium Hotels & Resorts, one of the oldest international-brand hotels in central Taiwan.
notes: Low English-language profile. Company site was unreachable during research (503), and the web-search budget ran out, so no deep-cut fact or press contact was verified. Robotics/automation angle. Reach via Apex Dynamics IR (TWSE filings) once site is reachable.

name: Hartono Kweefanus
current_role: Chairperson Emeritus and director, Monde Nissin Corporation (Philippines); chairman, PT Khong Guan Biscuit Indonesia
profile: Indonesian businessman whose late father co-founded Philippine food maker Monde Nissin (Lucky Me! noodles, SkyFlakes, Quorn meat substitutes) in 1979 with Betty Ang, his sister-in-law. A Monde director for 45 years and long its chairman, he is now Chairperson Emeritus, while also chairing Indonesia's PT Khong Guan Biscuit and other family companies. His wealth stems from his stake in Monde Nissin.
interesting_fact: Monde Nissin's June 2021 IPO raised $1.1 billion, at the time the Philippines' biggest ever; its Lucky Me! brand has been the country's most-chosen FMCG brand for a decade.
deep_cut_fact: He studied Industrial and Business Management at Nanyang University in Singapore, and besides Monde Nissin he chairs PT Khong Guan Biscuit Indonesia, the maker of the famous red Khong Guan biscuit tins.
notes: Very private; Kataline Darmono is now board chair and Henry Soesanto CEO. Food-manufacturing, not energy. Route via Monde Nissin IR. The 'red tin' descriptor of Khong Guan is general knowledge, not from the cited page.

name: Tran Ba Duong
current_role: Founder and Chairman, THACO (Truong Hai Group), Vietnam
profile: Born in Huế in 1960, Tran Ba Duong trained as a mechanical engineer, worked his way up from an auto repair factory, and founded Truong Hai Auto (THACO) in 1997. It grew from selling cars to assembling Kia, Mazda and Peugeot models, gaining Jardine Cycle & Carriage as an investor in 2008, and is now a conglomerate spanning autos, real estate, agriculture and logistics. He stepped down as CEO in 2013 but remains chairman.
interesting_fact: He won the EY ASEAN Entrepreneurial Excellence Award in 2020, and is known for controlling every detail, often calling management meetings on evenings and weekends.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated in mechanical engineering from Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology in 1983 and began as a repair technician at the Dong Nai auto repair factory before rising to management, so he literally went from fixing cars to building Vietnam's largest carmaker.
notes: THACO sites were unreachable (503/proxy errors) during research and web-search budget was exhausted, so no press email verified. Also linked to Dai Quang Minh real estate (Thu Thiem). Industrial/EV-manufacturing angle may suit podcast.

name: Ramesh Chandra
current_role: Founder of Unitech Group (no current executive role found; Unitech has been under a government-appointed board since 2020)
profile: IIT Kharagpur-trained structural engineer who in 1972 co-founded United Technical Consultants, a Delhi soil-investigation firm that became Unitech, once India's second-largest listed real-estate developer. He moved into civil engineering (including projects in Libya) and then housing, with Forbes putting his fortune at over $11B at its 2007 peak; he was a billionaire through 2011.
interesting_fact: Unitech began in 1972 as a soil-testing consultancy started by five partners before becoming a property giant building in Gurgaon and the Middle East.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Farrukhabad, Uttar Pradesh, the son of a banker, he worked briefly at the Bridge and Roof Company in Kolkata after IIT Kharagpur, then went to the University of Southampton to study structural engineering before co-founding his soil-investigation firm with four friends.
notes: Born c.1939-41; alive status not confirmed (no death reported on Wikipedia). Heavily entangled in legal cases (company and family) since 2011; Unitech under government-appointed management. Low suitability for outreach; no published personal contact found.

name: Robert Tsao Hsing-Cheng
current_role: Founder and former chairman of United Microelectronics Corp (UMC); civil-defence philanthropist and activist in Taiwan
profile: Born in Beijing in 1947 and raised in Taiwan, Tsao studied electrical engineering at NTU, worked at ITRI, and in 1980 founded UMC, Taiwan's first private chipmaker. He held Singapore citizenship 2011-2022 (hence the Singapore listing), then regained Taiwanese citizenship in 2022 and pledged NT$3B toward Taiwan's civil defence; he advised President Lai's Whole-of-Society Defense Resilience Committee (2024-25).
interesting_fact: After the 2019 Yuen Long attack in Hong Kong, Tsao vowed never to return to China, Hong Kong or Macau, and in 2022 pledged funds to train civilians and build a million combat drones for Taiwan's defence.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serious art collector who started in the 1990s with jadeite before moving on to archaic Chinese bronzes, and he recorded an oral history on the founding of UMC for the Computer History Museum.
notes: Outspoken and media-accessible (interviews with FT, RFA, Globe and Mail), so a podcast fit on semiconductors/geopolitics. No verified published contact found in budget; UMC press office (umc.com) is not his personal channel. Jadeite/bronze detail sourced via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Tsao (Christie's interview).

name: Liu Guowei
current_role: Early shareholder of Shenzhen Inovance Technology (largest individual shareholder in 2023, ~3%); no current executive role found
profile: Liu Guowei (刘国伟) was one of the early natural-person shareholders of Shenzhen Inovance Technology (SZSE 300124), China's largest industrial-automation company, founded in 2003 by Zhu Xingming and a group of ex-Huawei engineers. Inovance's 2023 annual report lists him as the largest individual shareholder (about 2.99%, ~80M shares), the source of his Hurun-listed fortune.
interesting_fact: Inovance, nicknamed 'Little Huawei', is China's largest industrial automation company and its second-largest domestic industrial-robot maker; it also supplies EV electric drive systems.
deep_cut_fact: Inovance's 2023 annual report company history shows he became a shareholder in an April 2006 restructuring, when he and 13 other individuals bought 61.68% of the company from its three original 2003 registrants; he took 6.17%.
notes: Very low public profile; no biography found (Baidu Baike blocked). Chairman Zhu Xingming is the public face of Inovance and a better podcast target for automation/EV drives/energy storage.
